itinerary: Day 1: Arrival at Islamabad, representative escorts to hotel
Day 2: Drive Islamabad to Chilas via KKH/Babusar (10-12 hrs)
Day 3: Chilas to Raikot Bridge, jeep to Tattu, trek to Fairy Meadows
Day 4: Acclimatization and exploration at Fairy Meadows
Day 5: Trek to Beyal Camp (2-3 hrs)
Day 6: Trek to Nanga Parbat Base Camp (6-7 hrs)
Day 7: Explore base camp area and nearby viewpoints
Day 8: Return to Fairy Meadows (approx 6 hrs)
Day 9: Trek back to Tattu, drive to Chilas
Day 10: Drive from Chilas to Islamabad
Day 11: Departure to home country
pros: Most complete 11-day itinerary with full base-camp push, not just a viewpoint hike
Dedicated acclimatization day (Day 4) plus staged ascent via Beyal Camp
Transparent tiered PKR and USD pricing by group size (PKR 200k-400k)
Porters carry 14kg luggage; satellite phone included for emergencies
Fixed-departure rate of $1,100 (31% off $1,600) for budget bookers
cons: Long 10-12 hr Islamabad-Chilas road day with no rest buffer
Bottled water excluded despite multi-day camping at altitude
Solo and small-group rates are steep (PKR 400k / $1,800 solo)
verdict: The most thorough Nanga Parbat base-camp option here, with real acclimatization and a true 6-7 hr base-camp trek rather than a meadow overlook. Best for travellers wanting the full mountaineering-style approach.
excludes: International airfare, personal equipment, travel insurance, visa fees, tips, extra baggage and bottled water.

itinerary: Day 1: Arrive Islamabad, met at airport, escorted to hotel
Day 2: Early air-conditioned coach/van drive to Chilas
Day 3: Drive to Raikot Bridge (3 hrs), jeep to Tato, 3-hr hike to Fairy Meadows
Day 4: 3-hr trek to Beyal Camp (a Nanga Parbat base camp)
Day 5: Hike back to Tato, jeep to Raikot Bridge, drive to Naran
Day 6: Return drive to Islamabad
Day 7: Breakfast, transfer to Islamabad airport
pros: Air-conditioned private coach/van for the long KKH drives
Mix of hotel and cottage accommodation rather than pure camping
All 6 breakfasts, lunches and dinners explicitly included
Gentler 7-day pacing suitable for less experienced trekkers
cons: Reaches only Beyal Camp (labelled a base camp), not actual Nanga Parbat base camp
No dedicated acclimatization day before the high trek
Priced at $1,400pp only on a 4-people-sharing basis, so solo/pairs pay more
verdict: A comfortable, well-fed Fairy Meadows + Beyal Camp trip rather than a true base-camp expedition. Good for travellers prioritising comfort and a shorter schedule over reaching the actual base camp.
excludes: Flights to/from Islamabad, Pakistan visa, and travel insurance.

itinerary: Day 1: Arrival day in Islamabad, Pakistan
Day 2: Islamabad to Naran/Chilas (461km, 8-9 hr drive)
Day 3: Drive and trek to Fairy Meadows (3300m, 6 hrs), jeep then 2-3 hr hike
Day 4: Trek to base camp (3500m), 6 hrs walking via Beyal campsite
Day 5: Trek back to Fairy Meadows (3300m), 6 hrs walking
Day 6: Travel back to Naran (6 hrs)
Day 7: Travel back to Islamabad (8 hr drive)
Day 8: Sightseeing day in Islamabad
Day 9: Departure day, fly back home
pros: Eight guaranteed fixed departures listed April-September 2026
All meals, permits, porterage and staff wages included
Reaches Nanga Parbat base camp at 3500m via Beyal campsite
Low $100 deposit to secure a booking
cons: No acclimatization day; base-camp push is the day after arrival at Fairy Meadows
Group size not stated on the page
Flat $1,600pp with no small-group or solo pricing breakdown
verdict: A fixed-departure, set-price trek that does reach base camp at 3500m on a tight back-to-back schedule. Solid for travellers wanting guaranteed dates, less so for those needing acclimatization.
excludes: International flights, travel insurance, visa fees, tips and souvenirs.

itinerary: Day 1: Islamabad city tour - Shakarparian, Pakistan Monument, Faisal Mosque, Daman-e-Koh
Day 2: Drive Islamabad to Chilas via KKH, lunch Besham
Day 3: Jeep Raikot Bridge to Tatu, 3-4 hr hike to Fairy Meadows
Day 4: Fairy Meadows - optional short hikes, community, stargazing
Day 5: Optional trek to Nanga Parbat Base Camp (3,850m)
Day 6: Fairy Meadows to Islamabad, hotel check-in
Day 7: Airport drop-off
pros: Defined small group of 4-12 participants
Includes an Islamabad city tour day before the trek
Accommodation noted as proper bathrooms and wooden huts at Fairy Meadows
Medium intensity with age 15+, accessible to families/teens
cons: Reaching Nanga Parbat base camp (3,850m) is only an optional Day 5 activity
No staged acclimatization plan around the high trek
From $1,700pp, the priciest of the comparable Fairy Meadows trips
verdict: A comfortable Fairy Meadows tour where the actual base-camp ascent is optional rather than guaranteed. Best for sightseers who want the meadow experience with a base-camp hike only if conditions and energy allow.
excludes: Page does not itemise exclusions; base-camp trek itself is treated as an optional add-on rather than a core inclusion.

itinerary: Day 1: 05:00 depart Islamabad for Chilas via Hazara Expressway, Lulusar, Babusar Top
Day 2: Drive to Raikot, 2-hr jeep to Tattu, 3-4 hr trek to Fairy Meadows, camp
Day 3: Hike to Bayal Camp and Nanga Parbat Viewpoint, visit Reflection Lake, camp
Day 4: Trek back to Tattu (2 hrs), jeep to Raikot, travel to Naran/Besham
Day 5: 08:30 breakfast, depart for Islamabad, optional Naran rafting
pros: Lowest-cost option with PKR tiers starting around 24,600
Domestic-focused Pakistani operator using Babusar Pass scenic route
Day 3 adds Reflection Lake and Nanga Parbat Viewpoint alongside Bayal Camp
Easy 2-3 hr one-way viewpoint hike suitable for casual trekkers
cons: Goes only to Bayal Camp/viewpoint, never to actual Nanga Parbat base camp
Inclusions/exclusions only stated as All-Inclusive, not itemised
Wide PKR 24,600-185,000 price range with unclear tier differences
Very early 04:00-05:00 starts and no acclimatization buffer
verdict: A budget, domestic Fairy Meadows weekend trip topping out at the Bayal Camp viewpoint rather than base camp. Best for Pakistan-based travellers wanting an affordable scenic getaway, not a full base-camp trek.
excludes: Not itemised; page only states packages are All-Inclusive, with optional extras such as Naran river rafting charged separately.
